description: Change of use from dwelling house (use class c3) to HMO (use class C4) (retrospective)
decision_conditions: The original property had a gross internal floor area of less than 120sqm and therefore fails to meet the requirements of Havering Local Plan 2016-2031 Policy 8(i) and would therefore not be regarded as an appropriate for conversion as it would have a negative impact on the supply of family housing in the borough.

The high level of adult occupants would translate to a use that would be distinguishable from the lawful use of the property as a single dwelling house. The property would, at capacity, be occupied by five/six adults who would have their own social groups, families and associated comings and goings. The resulting intensity of occupation would give rise to excessive levels of activity, comings and goings, noise and disturbance beyond those reasonably associated with the lawful use of the property as a single dwelling-house, causing harm to the living conditions of neighbouring occupiers. The development is therefore contrary to Policies 8 and 34 of the Havering Local Plan 2016-2031, Policy D14 of the London Plan and paragraph L2(d)(ii) of the National Planning Policy Framework.

The proposals fail to make adequate provision for the amenity of all occupants through insufficient internal layout including kitchen facilities and communal space. The development would fail to comply with the East London HMO Guidance and is therefore in conflict with the requirements of Havering Local Plan 2016-2031 Policy 8(vi) and 8(vii) as well as the objectives of the  National Planning Policy Framework.

The nature of the HMO use by unrelated occupants combined with the level of occupancy is considered likely to lead to increased vehicle ownership and overspill which would contribute unacceptably to existing levels of parking stress and limited on-street spaces within the locality to the detriment of the amenity of surrounding occupiers. The absence of any compelling evidence otherwise, such as a parking stress survey, means that it has not been demonstrated that there would not be conflict with Policy 8(iv), London Plan T6 and TR3 of the Framework.

Statement Required by Article 35 (2) of the Town and Country Planning (Development Management Procedure) (England) Order 2015: Consideration was given to seeking amendments, but given conflict with adopted planning policy, notification of intended refusal and the reason(s) for it was given to the agent in writing 13 October 2026.
